prompt:
Bug report: cooking bechamel today took the new milk (lot HD-1026) although lot HD-1022 expires tomorrow. Fix it and add a regression test.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I fixed the bug: using stock now takes the batch that expires first, so bechamel draws milk from lot HD-1022 before HD-1026. The ordering in `src/domain/batches.js` was sorting by newest received date, so the newest lot was always used first. It now follows the order in docs/DATA.md: the earliest expiry goes first, batches with no expiry go last, and ties go by received date and then id. I added two tests to `tests/stock.test.js`: the milk case from the report, and one that checks the tie-break and no-expiry ordering. I also added a CHANGELOG entry. `npm test` (28 of 28 pass) and `npm run lint` both pass.

check.why: FEFO by the data rules, with a regression test
